Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

This is the no-Bookshelf ablation: no cross-domain fish-control research shelf
is provided. Base controller proposals only on the task contract, current and
inherited guidance, sampled solver results, inherited optimizer logs, and
current rollout evidence. Do not search for or reconstruct the omitted shelf
from neighboring configurations or repository history.

I’m using the workspace’s `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill because this task changes the multi-wake target policy. I’ll first read its full instructions and `README.md`, then inspect the prescribed rollout keyframes and inherited evidence before touching the candidate.

The skill requires a scored visual comparison before any policy edit: shared prewarm, the best finite rollout, and the most informative failure, with image claims cross-checked against metrics and diagnostics. I’m now mapping all sampled/inherited evidence and reading the remaining workspace contract and guidance in full.

The assigned parent is the prefilled `optimizer_c6e3d5636464`; the four sampled solver rollouts are all finite target reaches, so there is no sampled termination-failure sheet in this workspace. I’ll still honor the visual comparison requirement by contrasting the best finite sample with the clearest performance regression and will explicitly avoid inventing unavailable failure evidence. Next I’m reading all four observations plus the parent’s inherited notes and exact policy deltas.

Per the skill, I’m inspecting the common held-fish prewarm before released trajectories. This image is only initial-condition evidence; I won’t attribute its wake phase or cylinder layout to any candidate.

The prewarm confirms a developed, merged staggered wake with the held fish upstream/right of the target and cylinders; that geometry is shared. I’m now reading release-to-capture sheets for the `2.1` energy-gain best sample and the exact `2.0` anchor, then the posterior-guard regression to separate trajectory effects from score noise.

The released sheets show all three candidates self-propelling diagonally into the developed wake and capturing without collision or domain exit. The `2.1` gain preserves the anchor corridor while reaching slightly sooner and with a visibly tighter lower excursion; the split posterior guard finishes via a lower correction. I’m cross-checking those claims now against the compact time series and nested diagnostics, especially relative velocity, joint saturation, effort, and load.

The cross-check supports a tradeoff, not a free gain: `2.1` improves capture (`73.86` vs `74.23`), mean distance (`2.480L` vs `2.561L`), and upstream-relative x speed (`0.06565` vs `0.06433`), but raises command energy by 1.7%, RMS force by 11.4%, RMS moment by 4.5%, and both joints still hit the `28` guard. The skill now requires me to record the visual diagnosis and falsifiable hypothesis before editing; I’ll document a single `2.05` midpoint probe intended to bracket route benefit against load.

The diagnosis and hypothesis are now recorded before the policy change, as required by the visual-first skill. I’m applying exactly one solver candidate: a one-field change to `oscillator_energy_gain=2.05`, leaving the observed steering map, orbit, tail phase, damping, and symmetric guard untouched. I’ll then add the corresponding cross-candidate lesson to inherited guidance.

The candidate and durable guidance lesson are both updated, so the workspace is no longer in the contract’s incomplete state. The new lesson records the exact benefit/cost boundary of gain `2.1` and warns against extrapolation or coupling it to the inherited guard/damping regressions. I’m now checking the final diffs, parameter-schema consistency, and the required check-runner invocation; I will not run formal CFD.
